gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Toybox Alpha Four's 75 × 80 × 90 mm build space is 0.54 L, against 5.83 L on the Bambu Lab A1 mini. At the $249 price each page lists, that works out to about $461 per litre of build space for Toybox and about $43 for the A1 mini. None of them says that Toybox refills now cost $15 per 500 g ($30/kg) or that Toybox says other 1.75 mm PLA also works.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides.com (Toybox vs. A1 mini), which gives the same two build sizes and a $249 A1 mini price but never computes volume or value per dollar. It mentions 'Printer Food refills' but gives no refill price and no running-cost comparison. Tom's Hardware, the page ChatGPT cited, came back to WebFetch as only the title and navigation, with the article body missing, so I could not check whether it has a cost or volume calculation. I did not open printingxyz, 3dprinterlab, findmy3dprinter or the other results.
decides: It confirms the A1 mini as the best overall pick. For the same $249 starter price it gives about 10.8 times the build volume, which answers the 'outgrown fast' catch. It also changes the Toybox row on our page: its catch currently says 'filament about $60/kg', but refills are now $30/kg, and Toybox says any 1.75 mm PLA works (for example Elegoo at $16.99/kg), so filament cost is no longer a reason to avoid Toybox. Toybox stays the pick for ages 5–8 because of its toy catalog, not because it is good value.
